title: City-pop record sleeve: flat empty pool, white wall, hard cast shadow, striped numerals (gacha event)
summary: One dominant pool cyan with pale sky, paper-white walls and plates casting hard deep-teal shadows, lemon reserved for the top rarity and the main button, hand-drawn striped numerals as the signature, everything tilted a few degrees like postcards pinned to a wall.

provenance.case: gacha-event v3 (白昼公馆「三点钟的泳池」): KV, event screen, recruit screen, ten-pull results and a 10 s recruit motion; an original fictional gacha game made to test whether a strong borrowed grammar beats a safe one.
provenance.lineage: 1980s Japanese city-pop record sleeves (Hiroshi Nagai, Eizin Suzuki): flat empty pools, white modernist walls, hard cast shadows, an afternoon with nobody in it. Borrowed: the grammar (flat planes, one dominant hue, hard shadows, emptiness). Never borrowed: their paintings, compositions, palms or any sleeve art.
provenance.borrow: Borrow grammar, never assets. Every shape is drawn in code; the one photograph used (a CC0 fan-palm photo) only became a cast-shadow silhouette.
provenance.rounds: v1 navy-and-brass nautical chart (owner: 'too ordinary'), v2 vermilion lighthouse (collided with the Steam case), v3 this pack. First pass of v3: 17 tool findings and 10 by eye; final: 0.
measured: Contrast: deep teal #083B40 on pool #22B8C2 is 4.9:1; on the 4-star deep pool #1AA3AD only 4.03:1 (12 findings in the first ten-pull pass), so 4-star cards are deep-teal plates with paper text instead.

64 px thumbnail against a generic dark UI kit: mean difference 118-141 (v1: 18-20), dominant hue share 0.35-0.69; part of that difference is light-on-dark, so the thumbnails were also read by eye: KV = striped numerals + pool grid, event = the lemon lane, ten-pull = one lemon card in the middle.
Signature sizes: KV numerals about 440 px high against 18-20 px body (22:1); banner name 140 px against 16 px.

pool.use: the dominant ground: pool water and screen grounds; deep-teal text on it (4.9:1)

pool_deep.use: windows and decoration only; never a text ground (deep teal is 4.03:1 on it)

sky.use: pale sky above the pool line, the sleeve's sky

paper.use: walls, postcards, plates, the white tube of the numerals

lemon.use: reserved: the top rarity, the main pull button, the active tab, the sun

ink.use: all text, hard shadows (at 26% opacity), the numerals' cast shadow, 4-star plates

wall_shade.use: the shaded side of the white wall

display.use: event titles, banner names, featured names (set italic: the sleeve's slanted lettering)

head.use: screen titles, tab names, buttons, card names

num.use: Latin kickers (tracked .3em), dates, counts and currency values

fonts.resolve: fonts query --text "<your copy>" --style gothic --weight 900 resolves Noto Sans SC from the catalog (covers the CJK roles); Barlow Condensed is Latin-only and not in the CJK catalog: check it with fonts measure --path <BarlowCondensed-Bold.ttf> --text "<Latin copy>"; a string it cannot cover switches whole to Noto Sans SC.
fonts.licence: All roles use SIL OFL 1.1 fonts.
fonts.lettering: The striped numerals are drawn as paths (digits 0-9 and : . - /), not a font; they are measured as a lettering slot.
fonts.note: Fonts are named, not bundled. --font-dir <dir> reads coverage and embeds the faces for --png and the browser check.

grammar: One dominant hue: pool cyan fills the screen; lemon is reserved for the top rarity, the main button and the active state.
Every plate casts a hard deep-teal shadow down-right (10-20 px at 1080p, 26% opacity); no blur, no gradient.
Plates, tabs, cards and buttons sit at small tilts (-5 to +5 degrees) like postcards pinned to a wall; text stays upright on its plate.
The signature is a code-drawn striped numeral (a time, a stage number, a date) at 1:10 or more against body text; let one plate overlap a corner of it.
Worlds become objects: stages are pool lanes, the limited banner is a record sleeve with the record sliding out, ten-pull results are a wall of postcards with the top pull at twice the size.
No characters are needed: identity comes from the pool-gear icon family (lifebuoy, cocktail glass, diving board, palm, record, tray, camera), each one flat layer plus a hard shadow.

procedural: striped numerals (layouts-citypop.cjs stripes()): three strokes 20/11/4 units, paper/pool/paper, over a deep-teal cast shadow, sheared -10 degrees
striped sun: a disc with four horizon bands cut out in the ground colour
pool tiles: a 64 px grid of paper lines at 22% (40 px inside the sleeve)
fan-palm cast shadow: fifteen blades from one crown, deep teal at 30%, only on walls and never under copy
pool-gear icon family: flat shape plus a 6-unit offset deep-teal shadow
recipes: Palm silhouette from a photograph: materials fetch --source met --id 264601 --name met-fanpalm; materials cut --file materials/raw/met-fanpalm.png --mode none --finish ink; then threshold the ink layer to 1-bit and pass it to the palm collage slot (deep teal, 30%).
Paper tooth for print: materials generate --generator paper --params '{"profile":"laid-cream","pxPerMm":4}' --seed 1, multiplied at 30-50% over walls only.
collage: The only collage is the palm shadow: a silhouette at 30% on the wall, never under copy (collage-cover).
No photographs of people; the empty pool is the subject.
materials.sources: Met Open Access CC0 (fan palm photograph, 1860s-70s, object 264601) for the optional silhouette; everything else is drawn.

grammar: Camera moves are hard pushes of 0.15 s in two steps (tilt down from sun to pool), never eased pans.
Elements enter with a 0.12-0.16 s overshoot and settle; nothing fades in.

Recruit sequence (10 s): sun bounces, two hard pushes down to the pool, a lifebuoy drops and ripples (flat rings), the numerals pop, a lemon full-screen hit, postcards slap onto the wall, the top rarity last.
Ripples and drops never land on copy or inside the numerals (a lifebuoy in 15:00 reads as an extra dot).
motion.flashLimit: At most one full-screen colour change per second (the lemon hit); under the WCAG 2.3.1 three-flashes limit.

guidance: 64 px distinctiveness (guidance, not a gate): shrink each screen to 64 px wide with the logo painted out and set it beside a generic dark UI kit. It should still read as pool cyan + one lemon object + a striped numeral; if it reads as 'another dark game UI', the grammar was lost. The pixel difference alone overstates it (light against dark): look as well.
Deep teal on the decoration-only deep pool is 4.03:1: never set text there.
A drawn object near the numerals must not read as a glyph (a lifebuoy inside 15:00 reads as a stop).
checks.note: The browser check runs on every render: plates overlap the numerals on purpose, so ink overlap and occlusion are measured, not em boxes.

examples.note: Screens of the case that stay example renders (their structure is the case's own, not a reusable layout): see docs/cases/gacha-event/ (README showcase).
